<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


11. MANDATORILY REDEEMABLE PREFERRED SHARES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April&nbsp;29, 2011, in conjunction with the sale of our Medicare Part&nbsp;D business, Universal American issued an aggregate of $40&nbsp;million of Series&nbsp;A Mandatorily
Redeemable Preferred Shares (the "Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares"), representing 1,600,000 shares with a par value of $0.01 per share and a liquidation preference of $25.00 per share. The
Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares pay cash dividends at the rate of 8.5% per annum and are mandatorily redeemable on the six year anniversary of the issue date. There is no ability to call these
securities before maturity except in the event of a change in control. The proceeds from the sale of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares were used to pay a portion of the existing indebtedness of the
Company prior to the sale and transaction expenses. We did not retain any proceeds from the sale of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. At the closing of the sale of our Medicare Part&nbsp;D
business, certain officers and directors of the Company collectively purchased an aggregate of $10&nbsp;million of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
accordance with ASC 480, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, because the issuance of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares imposes
an obligation on us requiring the transfer of assets, specifically, cash, at the redemption date, the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares are reported as a liability on the consolidated balance sheets,
with the related dividends reported as interest expense on the consolidated statements of operations. At December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014 we had accrued $0.7&nbsp;million of such dividends,
recorded in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Issue
costs of approximately $1.1&nbsp;million were capitalized in other assets and are being amortized over the six year term of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


12. LOAN PAYABLE  </B></FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


2012 Credit Facility  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&nbsp;2, 2012, we entered into a credit facility (the "2012 Credit Facility") consisting of a five-year $150&nbsp;million
senior secured term loan and a $75&nbsp;million senior secured revolving credit facility. In connection with the 2012 Credit Facility, we incurred loan origination fees of approximately
$5.8&nbsp;million, which were capitalized and amortized over the life of the 2012 Credit Facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
November&nbsp;4, 2013, we entered into an amendment to our 2012 Credit Facility, which suspended and replaced certain financial covenants beginning with the quarter ended
September&nbsp;30, 2013 through December&nbsp;31, 2014, with the original financial covenants reinstated effective January&nbsp;1, 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with the amendment, we prepaid all scheduled 2013 and 2014 principal payments, including the final 2013 payment due December&nbsp;31, 2013 of $3.6&nbsp;million and all
2014 scheduled payments totaling $14.3&nbsp;million. We also paid fees and expenses of approximately $0.5&nbsp;million, which we had capitalized in other assets and amortized over the term of the
amendment. </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


13. DISCLOSURES ABOUT FAIR VALUES OF FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We used the following methods and assumptions estimate the fair value of each class of financial instruments for which it is practicable to estimate that value: </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Fixed maturity investments available for sale:</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note&nbsp;6&#151;Fair Value Measurements above. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Short-term investments and Cash and cash equivalents:</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For short-term investments and cash and cash equivalents, the carrying amount is
a reasonable
estimate of fair value. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other invested assets:</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other invested assets consists of cost-basis equity investments which are carried at the lower of cost or fair
value, equity
securities which are carried at their current fair value of $6.4&nbsp;million and collateral loans. Other than the equity securities, the determination of fair value for these invested assets is not
practical because there is no active trading market for such invested assets and therefore, the carrying value is a reasonable estimate of fair value. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Series&nbsp;A mandatorily redeemable preferred shares:</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the Series&nbsp;A mandatorily redeemable preferred shares fair value
represents the
present value of contractual cash flows discounted at current market rates for securities of equivalent credit quality. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Loan payable:</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the loan payable, fair value represents the present value of contractual cash flows discounted at current spreads for
equivalent
credit quality. </FONT></P>

portion of each special cash dividend is recorded as a dividend payable liability expected to be paid in the future to holders of our restricted stock as such shares vest. This
liability was $1.6&nbsp;million and $1.2&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, respectively, and is included in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets. In addition,
pursuant to the terms of our 2011 Equity Award Plan, each dividend reduces the exercise price on outstanding stock options as of the ex-dividend date by the amount of the dividend. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Earnings per Common Share:</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under ASC 260, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Earnings Per Share</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, income (loss) from
continuing
operations is the trigger for determining whether potential common stock equivalents are dilutive or </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


15. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2011, we established the Universal American Corp. 2011 Omnibus Equity Award Plan (the "2011 Plan") to replace the 1998 Incentive Compensation Plan (the "1998 ICP"). The 2011 Plan is
the sole active plan providing for the granting of various types of equity awards, including stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, and other stock-based
awards and/or performance compensation awards. The 2011 Plan is administered by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors. The aggregate number of shares of common stock available for
awards under the 2011 Plan is 13,000,000. Universal American's stock-based compensation expense relates to the equity awards granted under the 2011 Plan as well as restricted stock and performance
share awards that were granted under the 1998 ICP. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Compensation
expense, included in other operating costs and expenses, and the related tax benefit were as follows: </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We recognize compensation cost for share-based payments to employees, directors and other third parties based on the grant date fair
value of the award, which we amortize over the grantees' service period in accordance with the provisions of </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Compensation&#151;Stock Compensation
Topic</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, ASC 718-10. We use the Black-Scholes valuation model to value stock options, except in the case of performance-based stock options, where we use a Monte Carlo valuation
approach. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><BR>
UNIVERSAL AMERICAN CORP. AND SUBSIDIARIES </B></FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


15. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Options
granted during 2015 included 279,000 performance-based options which vest ratably over a four-year period, but only if our stock price meets specified targets at the vesting
dates. Vesting is cumulative, such that if a stock price target is missed on a vesting date, but a subsequent stock price target is met on a future vesting date, all previously unvested shares would
then vest. These options were determined to contain a market condition for vesting under ASC 718&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Compensation&#151;Stock
Compensation</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, and were valued using a Monte Carlo valuation approach. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
total intrinsic value of stock options (the amount by which the market price of the stock on the date of exercise exceeded the exercise price of the option) exercised during 2015,
2014 and 2013 were $3.5&nbsp;million, $0.3&nbsp;million and $0.1&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
received proceeds of $9.5&nbsp;million, $1.9&nbsp;million, and $0.6&nbsp;million from the exercise of stock options during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013, and
2012, respectively. Such proceeds were primarily non-cash, as substantially all exercises were made on a net basis. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
of December&nbsp;31, 2015, the total compensation cost related to non-vested awards not yet recognized was $3.2&nbsp;million, which we expect to recognize over a weighted average
period of 2.2&nbsp;years. </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Restricted Stock Awards  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with our 2011 Equity Plan, we may grant restricted stock to employees, directors and other third parties. These awards
generally vest ratably over a four-year period; however during the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 we paid a portion of the annual bonuses in the form of restricted stock. The 2014 and
2013 awards vest under certain circumstances on the one-year and two-year anniversary of the grant, respectively. We generally value restricted stock awards at an amount equal to the market price of
our common stock on the date of grant, except in the case of performance-based awards, which we value using a Monte Carlo valuation approach. We recognize compensation expense for restricted stock
awards on a straight line basis over the vesting period. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A
summary of our non-vested restricted stock awards for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015 is set forth below: </FONT></P>

15. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION (Continued)  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Shares granted during 2015 included 371,000 performance shares which vest ratably over a four-year period, but only if our stock price meets specified targets at the vesting dates.
Vesting is cumulative, such that if a stock price target is missed on a vesting date, but a subsequent stock price target is met on a future vesting date, all previously unvested shares would then
vest. These shares were determined to contain a market condition for vesting under ASC
718&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Compensation&#151;Stock Compensation</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, and were valued using a Monte Carlo valuation approach. In addition, 480,000 shares were
granted during 2015 that only vest following a change-in-control transaction. </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Tax Benefits of Stock-Based Compensation  </I></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;ASC 718-10 requires us to report the benefit of tax deductions in excess of recognized compensation cost as a financing cash flow. We
recognized $0.1&nbsp;million, $(1.0) million and $0.4&nbsp;million of financing cash flows for these excess tax deductions for years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


16. UNIVERSAL AMERICAN CORP. 401(k) SAVINGS PLAN  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective April&nbsp;1, 1992, we adopted the Universal American Corp. 401(k) Savings Plan. The 401(k) plan is a voluntary contributory plan under which employees may elect to defer
compensation for federal income tax purposes under Section&nbsp;401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The employee is entitled to participate in the 401(k) plan by contributing through
payroll deductions up to 100% of the employee's compensation. The participating employee is not taxed on these contributions until they are distributed. Amounts credited to employee's accounts under
the 401(k) plan are invested by the employer-appointed investment committee. Currently, we match employee contributions with our common stock in amounts equal to 100% of the employee's first 1% of
contributions and 50% of the employee's next 4% of contributions to a maximum matching contribution of 3% of the employee's eligible compensation. Our matching contributions vest at the rate of 25%
per plan year, starting at the end of the second year. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants
have the option to transfer/reallocate at will, outside of blackout periods, both vested and unvested employer contributions invested in our common stock to any of the other
investments available under the 401(k) plan. The 401(k) plan held 1.4&nbsp;million shares of our common stock at December&nbsp;31, 2015, which represented 13% of total plan assets and
1.3&nbsp;million shares of our common stock at December&nbsp;31, 2014, which represented 14% of total plan assets. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally,
a participating employee is entitled to distributions from the 401(k) plan upon termination of employment, retirement, death or disability. 401(k) plan participants who
qualify for distributions may receive a single lump sum, have the assets transferred to another qualified plan or individual retirement account, or receive a series of specified installment payments. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
made discretionary matching contributions under the 401(k) plan of $1.7&nbsp;million in 2015, $1.8&nbsp;million in 2014 and $1.5&nbsp;million in 2013. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>F-55</FONT></P>

17. STATUTORY FINANCIAL DATA AND DIVIDEND RESTRICTIONS  </B></FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Statutory Financial Data  </I></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our insurance subsidiaries are required to maintain minimum amounts of statutory capital and surplus as required by regulatory
authorities. However, substantially more than such minimum amounts are needed to meet statutory and administrative requirements of adequate capital and surplus to support the current level of our
insurance subsidiaries' operations. Each of the insurance subsidiaries' statutory are at levels we believe are sufficient to support their currently anticipated levels of operation. Additionally, the
National Association of Insurance Commissioners, known as NAIC, imposes regulatory risk-based capital, known as RBC, requirements on insurance companies. At December&nbsp;31, 2015, all of our
insurance subsidiaries maintained ratios of total adjusted capital to RBC in excess of the "authorized control level." The combined statutory capital and surplus, including asset valuation reserve, of
our insurance subsidiaries, including those that are being sold to Nassau and are reported in discontinued operations, totaled $187.7&nbsp;million and $255.9&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31,
2015 and 2014, respectively. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, the insurance subsidiaries generated statutory net income (loss) of $25.6&nbsp;million, $(3.1) million and
$39.4&nbsp;million, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
HMO/Medicaid companies are also required to maintain minimum amounts of capital and surplus, as required by regulatory authorities and are also subject to RBC requirements. At
December&nbsp;31, 2015, the statutory capital and surplus of each of our HMO affiliates exceeds its minimum requirement and its RBC is in excess of the "authorized control level." The statutory
capital and surplus for our HMO/Medicaid affiliates was $98.4&nbsp;million and $94.0&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, respectively. Statutory net income for our HMO/Medicaid
affiliates was $9.0&nbsp;million, $10.4&nbsp;million and $14.2&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Based
on current estimates, we expect the aggregate amount of dividends that may be paid by our retained insurance subsidiary and HMOs to our parent company in 2016 without prior
approval by state regulatory authorities to be approximately $10&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Shareholder Dividend Restrictions  </I></FONT></P>

</UL>

restrictions:</FONT></P>

<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Delaware law, governing the payment of dividends, which provides that dividends can only be paid out of surplus. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>

18. RESTRUCTURING CHARGES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the last several years, we have initiated and executed various restructuring plans, as discussed below. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Workforce Reduction</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;In 2015, in connection with our continued efforts to reduce operating expenses, a workforce reduction plan was developed for
implementation in late 2015 and 2016. As a result, in the fourth quarter of 2015, we committed to a plan to reduce our workforce in targeted areas, resulting in a charge of $1.1&nbsp;million for
severance and other benefits related to this plan. </FONT></P>

18. RESTRUCTURING CHARGES (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2014, we made the decision to exit certain non-core markets in our Medicare Advantage business, stopped our participation in several underperforming ACOs, chose not to rebid on
certain APS Healthcare contracts and exited the New York Health Benefits Exchange, known as the Exchange. During the fourth quarter of 2014 we committed to staff reductions across all segments
continuing into 2015, resulting in a charge of $2.0&nbsp;million. During 2015, additional staff reductions related to this plan resulted in additional charges of $0.7&nbsp;million, which were also
paid during 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2013, in order to reduce expense levels across the organization in response to lower levels of business in APS Healthcare and membership in our Medicare Advantage plans, in
particular, and to help address the cost increase beginning in 2014 related to the Affordable Care Act's fee on certain health insurance premiums, a workforce reduction plan was developed for
implementation in late 2013 and 2014. As a result, in the fourth quarter of 2013, we committed to a plan to reduce our workforce in targeted areas, resulting in a charge of $7.1&nbsp;million for
severance and other benefits related to this plan. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
2015, we made payments of $3.8&nbsp;million in connection with these workforce reduction programs, and have $1.2&nbsp;million accrued at December&nbsp;31, 2015, which we
expect to pay in 2016. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New York Health Benefits Exchange Exit</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;During the fourth quarter of 2014, we made the decision to discontinue our participation in the Exchange,
effective January&nbsp;1, 2015. In connection with this decision, at December&nbsp;31, 2014, we accrued $0.8&nbsp;million related to certain contractual charges we are committed to paying in
2015 related to the Exchange. During 2015, we made payments of $0.7&nbsp;million in connection with this plan. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Facility Consolidation</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;During 2015, we recorded a restructure charge of $5.6&nbsp;million related to the sale of our APS Healthcare domestic
business. In connection with the sale, we retained certain office space which we have exited and certain Managed Behavioral Health, known as MBH, contracts which we have terminated and are operating
at a loss as the business runs off. Our restructure charge for facilities represents the estimated costs to close the facilities, including lease buyout costs and rent costs, net of estimated sublease
revenue, on non-cancellable leases prior to termination. The related leases run through 2021. The charge related to the MBH contracts represents the estimated operating losses on the terminated
contracts through the end of the contractual period, March&nbsp;31, 2016. We expect no additional charges under this APS Healthcare restructuring initiative. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><BR>
UNIVERSAL AMERICAN CORP. AND SUBSIDIARIES </B></FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


19. UNCONSOLIDATED SUBSIDIARIES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We account for our participation in the ACOs using the equity method. Gains and losses are reported as equity in losses of unconsolidated subsidiaries in the consolidated statements of
operations. Our net investment in the ACOs is reported in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. We recognized equity in losses of our unconsolidated ACOs of $9.6&nbsp;million,
$17.8&nbsp;million and $33.6&nbsp;million, for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
July&nbsp;30, 2015, CMS informed us that our 23 Medicare Shared Savings Program, or MSSP, ACOs which were active in 2014, generated $80&nbsp;million in gross savings for program
year 2014. This compares to $66&nbsp;million in gross savings for 2012/2013, the first program period of the MSSP, which comprised up to 21&nbsp;months and which we reported in the third quarter
of 2014. For these 23 ACOs, the program year 2014 results showed that:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 9 ACOs, serving more than 105,000 Medicare beneficiaries, including our flagship ACO in Houston, qualified for shared savings totaling
$26.9&nbsp;million. This compares to $20.4&nbsp;million in shared savings paid to ACOs for the first program year 2012/2013, which was longer. Our share of these payments, recorded in the second
quarter of 2015, after payments to our physician partners of $6.0&nbsp;million, increased to $20.9&nbsp;million, which is reflected in equity in losses of unconsolidated subsidiaries in our
consolidated statements of operations. We received these payments in October 2015; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 8 additional ACOs achieved savings but did not exceed the Minimum Savings Rate, known as MSR. Of those eight, four missed the MSR by
less than 1%; and </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Quality scores improved for all ACOs, which indicates improved healthcare management particularly for our chronically ill
beneficiaries. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
September 2014, we received notice that the ACOs we formed in partnership with primary care physicians and other healthcare professionals generated $66&nbsp;million in total
program savings for CMS, as part of the Medicare Shared Savings Program for the first performance year of the MSSP (2012 and 2013). Of our 30 ACOs with start dates in 2012 and 2013, the results showed
that:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 3 ACOs, serving more than 56,000 Medicare beneficiaries and including our largest ACO in Houston, generated savings in excess of their
Minimum Savings Rate and therefore, qualified to share those savings with CMS; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 11 ACOs, serving more than 120,000 Medicare beneficiaries, generated savings but fell below their Minimum Savings Rate required to
share savings with CMS; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 8 ACOs were within 2&nbsp;percent of their benchmark; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> 8 ACOs were 2&nbsp;percent or more above their benchmark; and </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> All ACOs met CMS's quality reporting standards. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
three ACOs qualifying for savings received payments of $20.4&nbsp;million, part to be shared between the physicians of those ACOs and us and part to be used by us to reimburse a
portion of the costs that we had incurred. Our share of these savings, including expense recovery, amounted to $13.4&nbsp;million, which is reflected in equity in losses of unconsolidated
subsidiaries in our consolidated statements of operations. We received these payments in October 2014. We did not recognize any shared savings revenue in 2013. </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


20. SALES OF SUBSIDIARIES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The following transactions relate to subsidiaries of our Medicare Advantage segment: </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sale of SelectCare of Oklahoma:</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On December&nbsp;31, 2014, we completed the sale of SCOK to Healthcare Investors,&nbsp;LLC. SCOK
operated as a
special needs HMO Medicare advantage plan in Oklahoma with approximately 120 members, representing approximately $3.2&nbsp;million of annualized revenue. The purchase price at closing was
$1.9&nbsp;million and was settled in cash. At the date of sale, the carrying value of SCOK included $0.4&nbsp;million of goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets that were disposed of in
connection with the sale. The transaction resulted in a pre-tax realized loss of $0.6&nbsp;million, or $0.5&nbsp;million after taxes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sale of Today's Options of Oklahoma:</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On August&nbsp;29, 2014, we completed the sale of TOOK to Momentum Health,&nbsp;LLC. TOOK
operated an HMO
Medicare Advantage plan in Oklahoma with approximately 5,800 members, representing approximately $63&nbsp;million of annualized revenue. The purchase price was $15.5&nbsp;million of which we
received $15.2&nbsp;million in cash at closing. The balance of $0.3&nbsp;million is
recorded as a receivable in other assets on the consolidated balance sheets and was settled in cash during the first quarter of 2015. At the date of sale, our carrying value of TOOK </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


21. DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The following transactions represent disposals or commitments to dispose of a reporting group and therefore they are reported as discontinued operations: </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sale of Traditional Insurance Business:</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On October&nbsp;8, 2015, we entered into a definitive agreement to sell our Traditional
Insurance business
to Nassau. Our Traditional Insurance business includes Medicare supplement, long term care, disability, life, and other ancillary insurance products, all of which have been in run-off since 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under
the terms of the agreement, Nassau will acquire Constitution and Pyramid, and reinsure the Traditional Insurance business written by Progressive through a 100% quota share
coinsurance agreement. The purchase price is approximately $43&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
purchase price is subject to adjustments based on actual capital and surplus of Constitution and Pyramid at closing, compared to the target statutory capital and surplus of
$68.5&nbsp;million. We will also be entitled to receive potential earn-out payments through June&nbsp;30, 2018 that may result in additional payments of between $13&nbsp;million and
$24&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Excluding
the impact of the earn out, based on projected capital and surplus, we currently expect to receive approximately $15&nbsp;million to $20&nbsp;million of net cash proceeds
at closing, which could change based on actual capital and surplus at closing. At December&nbsp;31, 2015, we have recorded a $133.8&nbsp;million adjustment, after tax, to write down the carrying
value of this business to estimated fair value. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
closing of the agreement is expected in the first half of 2016, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approval from the Texas, Kansas and New York insurance
departments and other third party reinsurer consents. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
of December&nbsp;31, 2015, in accordance with ASC 360-10 </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Property, Plant and Equipment</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> and ASC&nbsp;205-20 </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Presentation of Financial Statements&#151;Discontinued Operations,
</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> we determined that our Traditional Insurance business should be classified as
held for sale and reported in discontinued operations. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under
ASC 360-10-35, a long-lived asset classified as held for sale shall be measured at the lower of its carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell. We determined fair value at
December&nbsp;31, 2015, by calculating estimated net proceeds, using actual statutory surplus at December&nbsp;31, 2015, estimating the likelihood of receiving any earn out and estimating closing
costs. Estimated net proceeds were compared to the GAAP book value of the entities being sold and the business being reinsured at December&nbsp;31, 2015. Our analysis indicated a pre-tax loss of
$149.2&nbsp;million, generating a deferred tax benefit of $40.9&nbsp;million, against which we recorded a $25.6&nbsp;million valuation allowance. This resulted in an after-tax loss of
$133.8&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally,
discontinued operations treatment requires that the related assets and liabilities for the current period and all historical periods presented were reclassified as assets
and liabilities held for </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>sale
in our consolidated balance sheets, and the related operating results for the current period and all historical periods presented have been reclassified as discontinued operations in our
consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sale of APS Healthcare:</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On February&nbsp;4, 2015, we sold our APS Healthcare Puerto Rico subsidiaries to an affiliate of the
Metro Pavia Health
System. APS Puerto Rico provided managed behavioral health services under the Government Health Plan Medicaid program under a contract that terminated on March&nbsp;31, 2015 and had
$151&nbsp;million of revenue in 2014. The purchase price at closing was $26.5&nbsp;million, which was settled in cash. The transaction resulted in a pre-tax realized loss of approximately
$0.4&nbsp;million. The transaction also generated an additional foreign tax credit carryforward of $4.3&nbsp;million that has been recorded as a deferred tax asset. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
May&nbsp;1, 2015, we sold our remaining APS Healthcare operating subsidiaries to KEPRO,&nbsp;Inc., a company that provides quality improvement and care management services to both
government clients and the private sector. The purchase price was $5.0&nbsp;million, which was settled in cash at closing, subject to a working capital true up, which was finalized during the
quarter ended September&nbsp;30, 2015. In addition, the transaction includes a potential earn-out of up to an additional $19.0&nbsp;million based on certain contract renewals. Due to the
variability in the length of time over which the contract renewals may occur and the difficulty of estimating the success of such renewals, we consider the potential earn-out to be a contingent gain
which will be recorded only if and when we determine it to be realizable. At December&nbsp;31, 2015 no portion of the potential earn-out met the criteria to be accrued as a contingent gain. The
transaction resulted in a pre-tax realized loss of $17.0&nbsp;million, including the working capital true up. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with the sales of the APS businesses, we agreed to provide certain support services to the buyers under a transition services agreement, or TSA, until they can assume the
responsibilities directly. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, we provided support under the TSA agreements and recognized fee income of $2.9&nbsp;million. All TSA services are complete
as of December&nbsp;31, 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective
with the sale of our APS Healthcare businesses, in accordance with ASC&nbsp;205-20, the results of operations and cash flows related to APS Healthcare are reported as
discontinued operations for all periods presented. In addition, the related assets and liabilities have been segregated from the assets and liabilities related to our continuing operations and are
presented separately in our consolidated balance sheets as of December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, respectively. </FONT></P>

Legal Proceedings  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the matters discussed below, we are also subject to a variety of legal proceedings, arbitrations, governmental
investigations, including SEC investigations, audits, claims and litigation, including claims under the False Claims Act and claims for benefits under insurance policies and claims by members,
providers, customers, employees, regulators and other third parties. In some cases, plaintiffs seek punitive damages. It is not possible to accurately predict the outcome or estimate the resulting
penalty, fine or other remedy that may result from any current or future legal proceeding, investigation, audit, claim or litigation. Nevertheless, the range of outcomes and losses could be
significant and could have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>

<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


22. COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
October&nbsp;22, 2013, we filed a lawsuit in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware against funds affiliated with the private equity firm GTCR, known as GTCR,
David Katz, a former managing director of GTCR, and former senior management of APS Healthcare (Gregory Scott, Jerome Vaccaro and John McDonough, all such defendants, collectively, the "Defendants").
The lawsuit, which alleges securities fraud, multiple material breaches of contract and common law fraud, seeks substantial damages, including punitive damages. The lawsuit arises out of our
acquisition of APS Healthcare from GTCR in March 2012. The Defendants filed a motion to dismiss the complaint. In a decision issued on July&nbsp;24, 2014, the court denied the motion with respect to
the breach of contract claim. The court granted the motion with respect to the securities fraud claims and portions of the common law fraud claims on the ground that they did not provide enough detail
about each Defendant's specific role in the alleged fraud. On September&nbsp;22, 2014, the Company filed an Amended Complaint to provide additional details regarding each Defendant's role in the
alleged fraud. We are awaiting a decision from the court on the Defendant's motion to dismiss. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Governmental Regulation  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Laws and regulations governing Medicare, Medicaid and other state and federal healthcare and insurance programs are complex and subject
to significant interpretation. As part of the Affordable Care Act, known as ACA, CMS, State regulatory agencies and other regulatory agencies have been exercising increased oversight and regulatory
authority over our Medicare and other businesses. Compliance with such laws and regulations is subject to CMS audit, other governmental review and investigation, including SEC investigations and
significant and complex interpretation. CMS audits our Medicare Advantage plans with regularity to ensure we are in compliance with applicable laws, rules, regulations and CMS instructions. Our
Medicare Advantage plans will likely be subject to audit in 2016 and our Total Care Medicaid plan will be subject to audit in 2016. There can be no assurance that we will be found to be in compliance
with all such laws, rules and regulations in connection with these audits, reviews and investigations, and at times we have been found to be out of compliance. Failure to be in compliance can subject
us to significant regulatory action including significant fines, penalties, cancellation of contracts with governmental agencies or operating restrictions on our business, including, without
limitation, suspension of our ability to market to and enroll new members in our Medicare plans, termination of our contracts with CMS, exclusion from Medicare and other state and federal healthcare
programs and inability to expand into new markets or add new products within existing markets. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain
of our subsidiaries provide products and services to various government agencies. As a government contractor, we are subject to the terms of the contracts we have with those
agencies and applicable laws governing government contracts. As such, we may be subject to False Claim Act
litigation (also known as qui tam litigation) brought by individuals who seek to sue on behalf of the government, alleging that the government contractor submitted false claims to the government. In
2014 and 2015, Innovative Resources Group,&nbsp;LLC ("IRG"), a subsidiary of APS Healthcare, resolved three False Claims Act matters relating to IRG's historical contracts in Missouri, Tennessee and
Nevada. During 2015, we sold our APS Healthcare business. However, it is possible that we could be the subject of additional False Claims Act investigations and litigation in the future that could
have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations. </FONT></P>

<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> Medicare Advantage; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> MSO; and </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our
remaining segment, Corporate&nbsp;&amp; Other, reflects the activities of our holding company, our prior participation in the New York Health Benefits Exchange, known as the Exchange, and other
ancillary operations. Effective January&nbsp;1, 2015, we are no longer participating in the Exchange. A description of our business segments is as follows: </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare Advantage</B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;The Medicare Advantage segment contains the operations of our initiatives in managed care for seniors. </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> HMO plans: Our HMO plans are offered under contracts with CMS and provide all basic Medicare covered benefits with reduced member
cost-sharing as well as additional supplemental benefits, including a defined prescription drug benefit. We built this coordinated care product around contracted networks of providers who, in
cooperation with the health plan, coordinate an active medical management program. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> In connection with the HMOs, we operate separate Medicare Advantage Management Service Organizations that manage that business and
affiliated Independent Physician Associations or IPAs. We participate in the net results derived from these affiliated IPAs. </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> PPO plans: Our PPO plans are offered under contracts with CMS and provide all basic Medicare covered benefits with reduced member
cost-sharing as well as additional supplemental benefits, including a defined prescription drug benefit. This coordinated care product is built around contracted networks of providers who, in
cooperation with the health plan, coordinate an active medical management program. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2> PFFS Plans: Our PFFS plans are offered under contracts with CMS and provide enhanced health care benefits compared to traditional
Medicare, subject to cost sharing and other limitations. These plans have limited provider network restrictions, which allow the members to have more flexibility in the delivery of their health care
services than other Medicare Advantage plans with limited provider network restrictions. Some of these products include a defined prescription drug benefit. </FONT></DD></DL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;MSO</B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;Our MSO segment supports our physician partnerships in the development of value-based healthcare models, such as ACOs, with a variety of
capabilities and resources including technology, analytics, clinical care coordination, regulatory compliance and program administration. This segment includes our CHS subsidiary and affiliated ACOs.
CHS works with physicians and other healthcare professionals to operate ACOs under the Medicare Shared Savings Program. CHS provides these ACOs with care coordination, analytics and reporting,
technology and other administrative capabilities to enable participating providers to deliver better care and lower healthcare costs for their Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries. The Company
provides funding to CHS to support the operating activities of CHS and the ACOs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicaid</B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&#151;The Medicaid segment includes the operations of our Total Care Medicaid health plan, which we acquired on December&nbsp;1, 2013. Total Care
provides Medicaid managed care services to approximately 39,000 members in upstate New York. Total Care also participates in the Child Health Plus program for low-income, uninsured children. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
report intersegment revenues and expenses on a gross basis in each of the operating segments but eliminate them in the consolidated results. These intersegment revenues and expenses
affect the amounts reported on the individual financial statement line items, but we eliminate them in consolidation and they do not change income before taxes. The most significant items eliminated
relate to interest on intercompany loans which cross segments. </FONT></P>

<A NAME="toc_gm77801_1"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B><BR>  UNIVERSAL AMERICAN CORP.<BR>  (Parent Company)    <BR>    <BR>    NOTES TO CONDENSED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


1. BASIS OF PRESENTATION  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Except as otherwise indicated, references to the "Company," "Universal American," "we," "our," and "us" are to Universal American Corp., a Delaware corporation, and its subsidiaries. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Universal
American is a specialty health and life insurance holding company with an emphasis on providing a broad array of health insurance and managed care products and services to
people covered by Medicare and/or Medicaid. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
the parent company only financial statements, the parent company's investment in subsidiaries is stated at cost plus equity in undistributed earnings of subsidiaries since the date of
acquisition less dividends paid to the parent company by the subsidiaries. The parent company's share of net income of its wholly owned unconsolidated subsidiaries is included in its net loss income
using the equity method. These parent company only financial statements should be read in conjunction with the Company's consolidated financial statements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


2. MANDATORILY REDEEMABLE PREFERRED SHARES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April&nbsp;29, 2011, in conjunction with the sale of our Medicare Part&nbsp;D business, Universal American issued an aggregate of $40&nbsp;million of Series&nbsp;A Mandatorily
Redeemable Preferred Shares (the "Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares"), representing 1,600,000 shares with a par value of $0.01 per share and a liquidation preference of $25.00 per share. The
Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares pay cash dividends at the rate of 8.5% per annum and are mandatorily redeemable on the six year anniversary of the issue date. There is no ability to call these
securities before maturity except in the event of a change in control. The proceeds from the sale of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares were used to pay a portion of the existing indebtedness of the
Company prior to the sale and transaction expenses. We did not retain any proceeds from the sale of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. At the closing of the sale of our Medicare Part&nbsp;D
business, certain officers and directors of the Company collectively purchased an aggregate of $10&nbsp;million of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
accordance with ASC 480, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, because the issuance of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares imposes
an obligation on us requiring the transfer of assets, specifically, cash, at the redemption date, the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares are reported as a liability on the consolidated balance sheets,
with the related dividends reported as interest expense on the consolidated statements of operations. At December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014 we had accrued $0.7&nbsp;million of such dividends,
recorded in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Issue
costs of approximately $1.1&nbsp;million were capitalized in other assets and are being amortized over the six year term of the Series&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


3. LOAN PAYABLE  </B></FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


2012 Credit Facility  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March&nbsp;2, 2012, we entered into a credit facility (the "2012 Credit Facility") consisting of a five-year $150&nbsp;million
senior secured term loan and a $75&nbsp;million senior secured revolving credit facility. In connection with the 2012 Credit Facility, we incurred loan origination fees of approximately
$5.8&nbsp;million, which were capitalized and amortized over the life of the 2012 Credit Facility. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
November&nbsp;4, 2013, we entered into an amendment to our 2012 Credit Facility, which suspended and replaced certain financial covenants beginning with the quarter ended
September&nbsp;30, </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>F-75</FONT></P>

3. LOAN PAYABLE (Continued) </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>2013
through December&nbsp;31, 2014, with the original financial covenants reinstated effective January&nbsp;1, 2015. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with the amendment, we prepaid all scheduled 2013 and 2014 principal payments, including the final 2013 payment due December&nbsp;31, 2013 of $3.6&nbsp;million and all
2014 scheduled
payments totaling $14.3&nbsp;million. We also paid fees and expenses of approximately $0.5&nbsp;million, which we had capitalized in other assets and amortized over the term of the amendment. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
March&nbsp;31, 2015, we repaid $58.6&nbsp;million of principal on our term loan under the 2012 Credit Facility. On October&nbsp;9, 2015, we executed an amendment to our 2012
Credit Facility which waived certain financial covenants for the period ended September&nbsp;30, 2015. In addition, on October&nbsp;14, 2015, we repaid the outstanding balance on our term loan of
$44.9&nbsp;million and terminated the 2012 Credit Facility, including the unused revolver. In connection with the repayments, we recorded additional loan origination fee amortization of
$0.8&nbsp;million at March&nbsp;31, 2015 and the unamortized balance of $0.8&nbsp;million at October&nbsp;14, 2015. </FONT></P>

<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:10.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;" -->


Principal and Interest Payments  </I></B></FONT></P>

</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015, as discussed above, we repaid all $103.5&nbsp;million of the term loan principal and
made interest payments totaling $1.3&nbsp;million and other fee payments totaling $0.5&nbsp;million. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, we made no principal payments, interest
payments totaling $2.8&nbsp;million and other fee payments totaling $0.5&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


4. LOANS FROM AFFILIATES  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the fourth quarter of 2013, we borrowed $13.0&nbsp;million and $9.0&nbsp;million, at an interest rate of 3.5%, payable quarterly, from our insurance company subsidiaries,
Progressive and Pyramid, respectively, for general corporate purposes. On April&nbsp;10, 2015, we repaid the outstanding balance of $9.0&nbsp;million to Pyramid. The Progressive loan matures on
June&nbsp;30, 2016 and is repayable at any time without penalty. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;;margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;"><FONT SIZE=2><B>


<!-- COMMAND=STYLE_ADDED,"margin-left:0pt;text-indent:-0pt;" -->


5. SPECIAL DIVIDEND  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On October&nbsp;26, 2015, we paid a special cash dividend of $0.75 per share, to shareholders of record on October&nbsp;19, 2015. The total dividend was $63.0&nbsp;million. This
dividend is a liquidating dividend and was recorded as a reduction of additional paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
August&nbsp;19, 2013, we paid a special cash dividend of $1.60 per share, to shareholders of record as of August&nbsp;12, 2013. The total dividend was $142.1&nbsp;million. This
dividend is a liquidating dividend and was recorded as a reduction of additional paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A
portion of each special cash dividend is recorded as a dividend payable liability expected to be paid in the future to holders of our restricted stock as such shares vest. This
liability was $1.6&nbsp;million and $1.2&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2015 and 2014, respectively, and is included in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets. In addition,
pursuant to the terms of our 2011 Equity Award Plan, each dividend reduces the exercise price on outstanding stock options as of the ex-dividend date by the amount of the dividend. </FONT></P>
